purpose: library: the decennial census — conducted every 10 years in years ending in zero on Census Day, April 1; the first census in 1790 under George Washington led by Thomas Jefferson counted 3,929,625 people and apportioned 105 seats among 15 states; Article I Sections 2 and 9 and the Title 13 codification of 1954 with its notification deadlines (subjects three years before, question wording two years before); apportionment as the original legal purpose, the House fixed at 435 in 1913; redistricting after each census; and the 72-year confidentiality rule (records from 1950 and earlier at the National Archives). Fits quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the numbers and dates, a compare table of apportionment vs redistricting, and step ordering.
